recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future expansion of CarePlan.addresses to directly reference RiskAssessment or other risk-specific artifacts should be treated as a separate Patient Care decision, not as remaining FHIR-11170 work.
issue_request: FHIR-11170 was a Published Patient Care change request with a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution. It asked to include risk in the CarePlan structure, and the accepted resolution was to update CarePlan.addresses usage notes so the element can identify risks addressed by the plan as well as active conditions, with Condition able to represent examples such as "at risk for hypertension" or "fall risk".
initial_application: Git commit c124072d7bc14dd9eea48ac1aaf530bcd31171a6 applied #11170 to the old CarePlan spreadsheet source by adding the risk/active-condition wording to CarePlan.addresses requirements and marking the row GF#11170. Later migration commits moved that content into the current StructureDefinition XML, and FHIR-20168 refactored the element into code/reference guidance while preserving the risk semantics.
additional_context: CarePlan is active in source/fhir.ini and assigned to Patient Care. Current source/careplan/structuredefinition-CarePlan.xml is the authoritative current source for CarePlan.addresses; it says CarePlan.addresses.concept can describe a condition, problem, diagnosis, or risk, and its requirements say the element can identify risks addressed by the plan as well as concerns. Later work, including FHIR-32512 target-profile expansion and the FHIR-13743 allergy/intolerance restoration, does not supersede the risk guidance. Quoted FHIR-11170 Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community record; broader CarePlan risk hits concerned a separate RiskAssessment linkage question.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Adding a new risk element or duplicating the older examples would exceed the final resolution because the current active source already conveys that CarePlan.addresses can identify risks.

related_jiras.note: Later CarePlan.addresses refactoring added coded/reference guidance while preserving the ability to identify risks.
Later target-profile expansion explains the current Condition, Procedure, and MedicationAdministration reference targets without changing the risk guidance.
A separate later reconciliation restored allergy/intolerance CarePlan.addresses guidance and preserved the existing risk wording.
